analysis.title: [GS] Global Data Center Capacity Update, TODAY - Asia Healthcare Corporate Day
key_insights: S&P closed -51bps at 7,541. Momentum fell 6.7% while laggards rose 1% as the US 10yr (4.91%) and oil (WTI -8%) pressures eased. S&P Equal Weight outperformed SPX by about 125bps.
Semis (SOX) kept falling after closing below the 200-day moving average on Friday for the first time since June 2025.

GS floor activity was a 3 on a 1-10 scale. Asset managers were moderate net sellers, driven by tech. Hedge funds were moderate net buyers, with scattered cover demand in industrials, tech and healthcare, on muted notional.

GS (Michael Ng) now forecasts 273GW of global data center supply by 2030, versus 217GW in its July 2026 update. That implies 170GW of added capacity after 2025, with net additions of 25GW, 32GW and 35GW in 2026, 2027 and 2028.
For the US, GS forecasts 152GW of data center capacity by 2030 versus 125GW prior, or 103GW of additional capacity after 2025.

GS acknowledges rising execution risk in building data centers from power supply issues, regulatory uncertainty and high leverage. It still sees sustained outsized capacity growth in projects with visible power and permitting.

GS AI Adoption Tracker for October 2026 shows adoption among US establishments up 0.8pp to 24.6%, expected to reach 28.6% in the next 6 months. Equity analysts expect global semiconductor revenue of $872bn (annualized) by end of 2026.

AI is cutting employment in marketing, graphic design, customer service and some tech occupations. Construction jobs exposed to data centers are up 315k since 2022 relative to broader construction trends. Productivity gains are large in limited generative AI deployments but only modest economy-wide.

GS Korea Financials (Sinyoung Park) says the bank share correction has overshot the temporary fundamental softness. In GS's view the market is pricing recent NIM weakness as permanent when the drivers were transitory. Samsung Life drew the most questions after its hybrid issuance.

CXMT (688825.SS) is rated Buy. 3Q26 gross margin rose to 90%, DDR5 mass production is ramping, and LPDDR6 has been adopted by smartphone brand clients. The company is verifying DDR6 engineering samples and has developed a 4F^2 architecture on its VSG technology.
MediaTek (2454.TW) is rated Buy with TP raised to NT$7,100. Its first AI ASIC project is contributing revenue gradually, the second project has some dies taped out, and 4Q26 guidance is in line.
Innolight (300308.SZ / 3308 HK) is rated Buy. The 1.6T ramp should drive growth, with 3Q26 revenues and gross margin rising sequentially.

Rating changes: Sirius XM (SIRI) upgraded to Buy, Floor & Decor (FND) downgraded to Sell on lower FY26 guidance and moderating 2027 unit growth, and Skshu Paint (603737.SS) cut to Sell after a 3Q26 miss.

GS Goal Kickstart headline reads 'Tech wreck - rotation out of AI stocks continues into midterm elections'. Other popular notes cover Apple's F4Q26 EPS beat, Marvell's agreement to acquire Lumentum, and a raised GS oil price forecast on high supply disruption risk.
GS hosts three midterm election calls on Nov 4: 8am ET first take, 10:15am ET views from DC and the trading floor, 11:30am ET election post mortem.

market_movers.rationale: CXMT 3Q26 beat with gross margin up to 90%. 4Q26 and 2027 revenue should keep growing on DDR5 and LPDDR6. No US listing.
MediaTek AI ASIC ramp has stronger momentum, with the next-gen project on track and new clients being added. 4Q26 guidance is in line.
Innolight 1.6T ramp should drive growth, with 3Q26 revenues and gross margin rising sequentially.
Improving risk/reward from durable core satellite trends, ramping YouTube monetization and potential spectrum value unlock.
Moderating 2027 unit growth, and management lowered FY26 guidance amid macro pressures.
Skshu Paint 3Q26 miss, with persistent demand weakness fueling competition and delaying growth recovery.

sector_views.rationale: Bank share correction has overshot temporary fundamental softness, and NIM weakness is priced as permanent when the drivers were transitory.
Capacity forecasts raised to 273GW globally by 2030, with sustained growth in projects that have visible power and permitting.

earnings_insights: CXMT (688825.SS) 3Q26 beat per GS, gross margin up to 90%. The note gives no EPS or revenue figure.
MediaTek 4Q26 guidance is in line with GS expectations. TP raised to NT$7,100.
Innolight 3Q26 revenues and gross margin rose sequentially, per GS.
Apple F4Q26 first take: EPS beat on iPhone, Mac and gross margins (headline only, no figures given).
Floor & Decor lowered FY26 guidance, which led to GS's downgrade to Sell.

Oil pressure eased in the session, alongside lower yields.
Up 0.8pp month over month, supporting continued AI-related investment.

Equity analyst expectation, indicating AI investment strength in semis.

risk_factors: Data center build-out faces power supply issues, regulatory uncertainty and high leverage.
Tech correction and continued foreign net selling weigh on Korean financials.
Rotation out of AI stocks continuing into the midterm elections.
Oil supply disruption risk, which GS cites in raising its price forecast.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum factor fell 6.7% on the day while laggards rose 1%, a sharp factor rotation.
SOX closed below its 200-day moving average on Friday for the first time since June 2025 and continued lower.
Asset managers were moderate net sellers (tech-driven) and hedge funds moderate net buyers, with scattered cover demand in industrials, tech and healthcare on muted notional.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on Nov 4, with GS hosting three calls on the outcome and a US Economics Analyst preview.
GS raised its oil price forecast on high supply disruption risks.
